title: PUT /youtube accepts non-positive max_items and persists it

evidence.quote:
if update.max_items is not None:
        feed.max_items = update.max_items

reasoning: The route forwards the request body to the shared updater, and the updater persists any non-null max_items value without a lower-bound check. The field represents a maximum item count, so values such as -1 or 0 are invalid or at least contract-ambiguous. In the inspected processing path, this value is later used as a feed parsing limit, so a bad persisted value can make an active YouTube feed ingest an unintended number of entries or none at all.
reproduction: With an existing YouTube feed, send PUT /api/media/youtube/{feed_id} with JSON {"max_items": -1}. The handler reaches _update_media_feed and persists -1 instead of returning a validation error.
recommendation: Reject non-positive max_items at the request schema boundary, for both create and update schemas if they share the same invariant, and consider a defensive check in _update_media_feed before assignment.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this route, and the inspected media API tests cover retry endpoints rather than YouTube feed update validation.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add an API test that creates a YouTube feed, calls PUT /api/media/youtube/{feed_id} with max_items=-1, and asserts 422 or 400 plus no persisted change; also assert a valid positive max_items update still succeeds.
minimumFixScope: Media feed request validation for max_items and a focused PUT /youtube/{feed_id} regression test.
